thread:
jonathan_infra: Heads up — eu-west GPU pool is hitting ~96% slot utilization for the streaming lane and we're seeing non-streaming queues ballooning (embedding & offline reranks). Some customers reported 503s.

emma_ops: noticed this on the dashboard too, live tail shows many streaming connections pinned on the same 8gpu instance group. any idea what's triggering the spike?

jonathan_infra: looks like a traffic shift from a single enterprise tenant doing interactive sessions + a few low-priority batch jobs that never got backpressured. streaming requests are sticky because of long-lived connections + large KV caches.

ravi_runtime: digging in — preliminary: our admission controller currently prefers streaming up to 90% capacity and preempts non-streaming only when >92%. That margin is too tight when several long-connections align.

olga_networks: also seeing increased retransmits on the node NICs in the same AZ which amplifies token hold time. packets/sec and RX drops correlate with the tail latency rise.

ciara_product: we have two customers on the low-latency plan; they expect streaming to keep priority, but several SME customers for embeddings are paying for batch throughput. we need short-term mitigation + a policy change.

jonathan_infra: short-term: can we apply a soft cap to per-connection streaming concurrency and reduce sticky KV windows? maybe reclaim idle streams earlier.

ravi_runtime: agree. temporary knob patch I can push: lower streaming_preempt_threshold to 0.85 and enable aggressive idle_kv_timeout=30s for sessions idle >30s. quick snippet:

```
# admission policy delta (temp)
admission:
  streaming:
    preempt_threshold: 0.85
    max_conns_per_user: 8
    idle_kv_timeout_s: 30
  non_streaming:
    queue_priority: 0.6
```

emma_ops: will run the patch in canary eu-west-1a now. starting with one node-pool.

sre-bot: deploy started by ravi_runtime at 1892016905 — canary -> eu-west-1a (1/3 nodes).

olga_networks: if NIC drops are the bottleneck, we might need to move some heavy KV-backed streams to different instance families with better pcie lane balance. that's a slower ops change.

ravi_runtime: patch is live in canary. monitoring: streaming slots down ~4% and non-stream queues decreased ~30% in the canary pool. good sign.

ciara_product: worth noting: lowering preempt makes streaming tail latency increase for a few users. product ok with that as long as we avoid 503s.

jonathan_infra: mid-term options: 1) dynamic burst pool (on-demand GPUs) that we spin up when sustained streaming occupancy >90% for >2m; 2) implement ephemeral "burst_lease" tokens that let non-streaming borrow capacity for short windows; 3) stricter per-tenant streaming concurrency + quota. need cost tradeoffs.

emma_ops: cost note: on-demand GPUs in eu-west are ~3x reserved per-hour. burst pool would resolve SLOs but double runcost for those minutes. need approval for budget runway.

ravi_runtime: prototyping lease idea — proposal: lease grants up to N tokens for T seconds to non-streaming jobs; controller retracts lease if streaming demand rises. naive YAML:

```
burst_lease:
  enabled: true
  max_lease_tokens: 200
  lease_duration_s: 45
  retract_threshold: 0.92
  retract_policy: immediate|graceful(5s)
```

jonathan_infra: I like lease because it smooths short spikes without heavy capex. risk: if retract is immediate, we will preempt mid-step jobs and cause retries. graceful retract buys a few seconds to drain.

olga_networks: if we introduce leases, we should couple them with egress rate shaping per pod to avoid NIC saturation. small per-pod qdisc throttles help.

ciara_product: can we prioritize paid batch (committed contracts) above free embed jobs during lease periods? that solves fairness for revenue customers.

ravi_runtime: yes — simple priority tiers. we can make lease allocation tier-aware.

emma_ops: can we add a quick alert to paging if eu-west streaming occupancy >95% for 3m? want humans involved before adding costly on-demand bursts.

jonathan_infra: agreed. action items:
- ravi_runtime: keep canary config live and roll to eu-west if stable (15m watch)
- olga_networks: investigate NIC drops and recommend instance families (ETA 3h)
- emma_ops: add alert rule for sustained >95% streaming occupancy (oncall)
- ciara_product: list tenants eligible for priority lease (legal/contract)

ravi_runtime: will follow up with PR containing lease prototype and rollout plan.

sre-bot: monitoring note — canary metrics show improvement in canary pool after config change. further rollouts require change review.

jonathan_infra: thanks all. if the canary degrades we revert. will update thread with follow-ups. :thumbsup:
